back: A list of characters a computer can represent, each with a **unique binary code**.
7 bits per character → 128 characters (extended ASCII: 8 bits → 256).
More bits per character (up to 32): almost every language plus emojis; first 128 codes = ASCII.

front: Why does Unicode need more bits?
back: More bits give more unique codes, so it can represent many more characters; the cost is larger files.
A lower-case letter's code is 32 more than its capital (A 65, a 97).
As a sequence of character codes in binary, one code per character (spaces and punctuation included).
Number of characters × bits per character.
The character "7" is code 55, not 7; text must be converted before arithmetic.
